facts.text: Midway up the buttress the rock splits at a gully: the left branch is more exposed with class 4 moves and looser rock, the right branch is simpler class 3 on scree.

Fixed anchors on the lower buttress allow three short rappels on the way down, though only the last one, onto the snow, is really needed. One 60 m single-rope rappel joins the upper two stations; a 50 m rope falls a few feet short.
In early July snow runs right to the first rock, and a waterfall beside the col camp runs in the afternoon (it may fade later in summer).
The summit crest has three bumps; tag the northern and middle ones, since parties disagree which is highest.
On the way out in early July the river runs higher after hot days and snow is slushy with some postholing; the muddy slabs and root path into the lower basin are the slickest part of the descent.

notes: North Ridge and Southeast Face have no qualifying in-season track (nothing logged names them). North Ridge has no Trailhead pin stored; if a track is later assigned, the Eldorado trailhead pin used by the other two routes (48.4926,-121.1222) would be the one to add, but I did not propose it without a track. Peakbagger summit coordinate (48.554512,-121.104563) agrees with SW Buttress pin within ~15 m.
